- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is trending down, reduce downward bias — model tends to overcorrect.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — model overreacts to pessimism.
- If recent history shows sharp declines followed by rebounds, model often overshoots the true low — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent low.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7) and forecast is volatile, apply mean reversion: smooth 3–5 day moving average to dampen noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of historical mean, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment spikes after a forecast dip, model often fails to recover — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to reflect sentiment momentum.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of 30-day historical low unless sentiment confirms strong bearish trend — otherwise, model underestimates downside risk.
